a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT — The standard practice delivers a vibration amplitude monitoring scheme (class: MONITORING/INDICATION) that triggers when overall vibration exceeds a fixed threshold. Our departure is a same-class mechanism that monitors the evolution of vibration harmonics specific to bearing defect frequencies rather than overall amplitude, detecting incipient spalling before it generates significant overall vibration increase.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the modulation of bearing defect frequencies by the shaft rotation frequency: f_mod = n × f_shaft ± f_defect, where n is the modulation order. For a bearing with ball pass frequency inner race (BPFI) of 150 Hz and shaft speed of 30 Hz, the first modulation sideband appears at 180 Hz (150 + 30) and 120 Hz (150 - 30). The magnitude verification shows that incipient spalling creates these sidebands at levels 10-15 dB below the main defect frequency, detectable with 1 kHz sampling.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
1. Same-class vibration sensor (existing 1 kHz accelerometer) — USER CONSTRAINT: problem states existing sensor
2. Signal processing module (off-the-shelf FFT analyzer) — SAME CLASS as standard practice's vibration monitoring equipment
3. Algorithm implementation (software running on existing SCADA system) — SAME CLASS as standard practice's monitoring system
4. Defect frequency calculator (bearing geometry database) — ASSUMPTION: bearing geometry is available in maintenance records

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Installability: SAME (uses existing sensor and SCADA infrastructure)
- Operability: SAME (no additional operator training required beyond standard vibration monitoring)
- Maintenance: SAME (no additional maintenance requirements)
- Cost class: SAME (no new hardware required, only software implementation)
- Conclusion: SAME burden class, different mechanism (harmonic evolution vs. amplitude threshold)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: 
1. Install test bearing with seeded inner-race defect in 350 kW fan drive
2. Monitor vibration at 1 kHz sampling rate while logging 1 Hz SCADA data
3. Record time-to-failure and time-to-alarm for both standard amplitude threshold and harmonic evolution method
4. Repeat for 10 bearing tests to establish statistical reliability

Instruments: 
- 1 kHz vibration accelerometer (existing)
- SCADA logging system (existing)
- Bearing defect frequency calculator

Pass/Fail Threshold: 
- Must detect defect at least 14 days before failure (USER CONSTRAINT)
- Maximum 2 false alarms per year (USER CONSTRAINT)

Duration: 
- Test until bearing failure or 30 days of operation, whichever comes first

Kill Criterion: 
- Failure to achieve 14-day warning in any of 10 tests
- More than 2 false alarms in cumulative test time
- Implementation requires new hardware beyond existing sensor and SC
